nodes.name: Fetch applications
nodes.notes: retryOnFail + maxTries + waitBetweenTries is n8n's equivalent of retry.py. The error output is the dead letter path.

nodes.name: One item per applicant
nodes.notes: Same reason as steps/ingest.py: one bad applicant must not fail the batch.

nodes.name: Screen
nodes.notes: Four outputs, matching steps/screen.py: invalid, accepted, review, rejected. 'review' ends here and waits for a human.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO submissions (external_id, email, handle, platform, followers, status, raw, created_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, 'accepted', $6, now())
ON CONFLICT (external_id) DO NOTHING
RETURNING id;

nodes.name: Store applicant
nodes.notes: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on a UNIQUE external_id is the whole of idempotency: re-running the batch stores each applicant once.

nodes.name: Send welcome email
nodes.notes: Sent after the creator row exists, so a failure here replays cleanly: the insert is a no-op and only the email is retried.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO posts (creator_id, platform, external_id, url, published_at, views, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
SELECT c.id, c.platform, $2, $3, $4, $5, now(), now()
FROM creators c WHERE c.tracking_code = $1
ON CONFLICT (platform, external_id) DO UPDATE
  SET views = EXCLUDED.views, last_seen_at = EXCLUDED.last_seen_at;

nodes.name: Upsert posts
nodes.notes: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on (platform, external_id). Without it, polling the same post twenty times would be paid twenty times.

parameters.query:
-- Recomputed from posts, never accumulated, and in integer cents.
INSERT INTO payouts (creator_id, period_start, period_end, post_count, total_views, amount_cents, computed_at)
SELECT c.id, $1::date, $2::date, COUNT(p.id), COALESCE(SUM(p.views), 0),
       (COALESCE(SUM(p.views), 0) * c.rate_cents_per_1k + 500) / 1000, now()
FROM creators c
LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.creator_id = c.id
  AND p.published_at >= $1::date AND p.published_at < $2::date
WHERE c.status = 'active'
GROUP BY c.id, c.rate_cents_per_1k
HAVING (COALESCE(SUM(p.views), 0) * c.rate_cents_per_1k + 500) / 1000 >= 100
ON CONFLICT (creator_id, period_start, period_end) DO UPDATE
  SET post_count = EXCLUDED.post_count,
      total_views = EXCLUDED.total_views,
      amount_cents = EXCLUDED.amount_cents,
      computed_at = EXCLUDED.computed_at;

nodes.name: Compute payouts
nodes.notes: Integer arithmetic end to end. ON CONFLICT makes a second run for the same period an update, not a second payout.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO dead_letters (task_id, kind, payload, attempts, error, reason, created_at)
VALUES (0, $1, $2, 1, $3, 'permanent', now());

nodes.name: Dead letter
nodes.notes: Every error output lands here. A row, not a log line, so it can be replayed once the cause is fixed.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ text: `creator-program: ${$input.all().length} item(s) dead lettered in run ${$execution.id}` }) }}

nodes.name: Alert once per run
nodes.notes: executeOnce is the point: an outage fails every item, and thirty failures must not send thirty messages. A broken alert channel never fails the run.
